title: The light placed in you
hook: the body came into the world when the Lord placed His light within it (Anand, the body pauris)

segments.voice: Yesterday, O my body, the Anand asking the body what it has done in this world. Did you thank one part of yourself? Today the next pauri speaks to the body again, and tells it where it came from. Day three hundred ninety-five.
screen: `O MY BODY — WHAT HAVE YOU DONE?`

segments.voice: A dim room, a gray screen, two parents holding hands. The technician moves the wand and points: there. A tiny flicker, fast as a bird's wing. Many parents say that moment changed something; before it there was news, and after it there was someone. Nobody in the room could tell you exactly what had arrived. The Anand has an answer, and it's the next thing Guru Amar Das says to the body. Today: the light placed in you.
screen: `A SCREEN, A FLICKER, TWO PARENTS.` → `BEFORE: NEWS. AFTER: SOMEONE.` → `WHAT ARRIVED?`

segments.voice: The pauri starts the same way as yesterday's, ae sareeraa mairiaa, O my body. But this time it doesn't ask what the body has done. It tells the body something. In paraphrase: the Lord placed His light within you, and then you came into the world. And it says it twice, turning the line around, as if to make sure it's heard. The Gurmukhi word is jot, light, the same word Sikhs use when they say the one light passed from Guru Nanak to each Guru after him. Here that light is placed in every body. Notice the order. First the light, then the arrival. The body doesn't earn the light later by being good; it comes into the world because the light is already in it. The pauri goes on: the Lord is Himself mother and Himself father, the One who made living beings and showed them the world. And by the Guru's grace, someone understands, and then the whole world is seen as a play, chalat, the Lord's own wonderful display. It closes with Guru Amar Das's signature line: the One who made the root of creation placed His light in you, and then you came into the world. Yesterday's question was hard: what have you done? Today's line is the ground under it. Whatever the body has or hasn't done, the light was placed there first. Many Sikhs hear this as the reason no one can be looked down on. Every body in the room arrived the same way. Light in the body.
screen: `O MY BODY, AGAIN: NOT A QUESTION NOW.` · `JOT: THE LORD'S LIGHT, PLACED IN YOU.` · `FIRST THE LIGHT, THEN THE ARRIVAL.` · `MOTHER AND FATHER, AND THE WORLD A PLAY.` · then, large: `LIGHT IN THE BODY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: feel your pulse. Lay two fingers lightly on the inside of your wrist, below the thumb, or at the side of your neck under the jaw. Wait until you find it. Don't count. Just feel it arrive, again and again, without being asked. You didn't start it and you aren't running it. Let that be enough for a while. If the Anand's line helps, let it ride along with the beat: light in the body. If you pray, you can say Waheguru once, softly. The bell holds the time.
The light placed in you. In the Anand, the Lord places His light, jot, in the body, and only then does the body come into the world.
screen: `THE LIGHT PLACED IN YOU — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: light in the body. Today, feel your pulse once more, maybe in a queue or before you sleep, and remember what the pauri says came first. Day three hundred ninety-five.

howItsDone: Many Sikhs recite the full Anand Sahib each morning, and the teaching that the one divine light, jot, dwells in every body is often given as a reason Sikhs reject caste and serve all in langar alike.

fork.setup: the Anand tells the body how it came into the world. what does it say came first?
options: the body, and the light was added at a ceremony.
the light, and then the body came into the world.
good deeds, and the light was the reward.
fork.reveal: the pauri says the Lord placed His light in the body, and then it came into the world: the light is there before anything is done.

original.note: Gurmukhi: jot, light; the Lord's light placed in the body, and the light Sikhs say passed through the ten Gurus.

trapdoor: what you thought: the light placed in you is a poetic way of saying you're special.
what it means: the Lord's own light is in every body, placed there before it came into the world.
what a scholar hears: jot is a key term across the Guru Granth Sahib; the same word underlies the Sikh teaching that one light passed through all ten Gurus.

sources.ref: Ramkali M3, Anand, the light pauri (ae sareeraa mairiaa har tum meh jot rakhee), Ang 921

notes: The light pauri paraphrased: Lord placed His light in you, then you came into the world (said twice); Lord is mother and father; by the Guru's grace the world is seen as a play (chalat); He made the root of creation. Commonly numbered pauri 35. Confirm numbering, Ang and glosses.
'Many Sikhs hear this as the reason no one can be looked down on': an interpretive link to the rejection of caste; confirm phrasing.
